{{Quote|Kavas ordered an old-style camera as a gift for Ind. We mixed it in with a shipment of spice from Aeten II... and there was a whole mess... I don't have time to go into details.|[[Ki'shai]], to a spacer|<ref name="SWG:KU">{{SWGcite|exp=AED|type=static|Kavas Urdano|Tatooine}}</ref>}}
'''Aeten II''' was a [[Planet/Legends|planet]] located in [[Wild Space/Legends|Wild Space]] of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] and was known primarily for its [[Stygium/Legends|Stygium]] [[Crystal/Legends|crystals]], which could be used to create [[Cloaking device/Legends|cloaking devices]] or as [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] crystals which gave a [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] increased stealth and dexterity. The planet was [[Destruction of Aeten II|destroyed]] in [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]], shortly following the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]], by [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] [[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admiral]] [[Martio Batch]], using the [[Tarkin (superweapon)|''Tarkin'']] [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapon]].

==History==
During the time of the [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]] between the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]] and [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] Aeten II, located in [[Wild Space/Legends|Wild Space]], was represented in the [[Rift Alliance]] by the [[Sullustan/Legends|Sullustan]] [[Diab Duin]].<ref name="TOR">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]''</ref> The Sith Empire established a [[Space station/Legends|space station]] in the planet's [[Orbit/Legends|orbit]]. Near the end of the Cold War, two Imperial traitors infiltrated the Sith Empire's space station and disabled its defenses. The agents were eventually neutralized, though their efforts left the station defenseless; this allowed a Republic fleet to attack and capture the station.<ref name="Aeten Defense">{{TORcite|type=space|Aeten Defense}}</ref>

Aeten II was later settled by the Galactic Republic, circa [[1000 BBY/Legends|1000 BBY]]. Eventually, the new inhabitants discovered the vast resources of stygium within the planet and rapidly built mines to extract the valuable [[Mineral/Legends|mineral]]. In [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]] however, shortly before the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]] passed a law restricting the export of stygium crystals, although the supply of crystals had utterly came to a halt due to the over-mining of reckless profiteers. Nonetheless, prospectors found new resources to mine.

[[File:AetenSurface.jpg|thumb|left|200px|AT-ST surveying an abandoned mining facility on the surface.]]
During the [[20 BBY/Legends|last year]] of the Clone Wars, Aeten II was the site of the month-long [[Battle of Dreighton]]. Both the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], aided by the [[Pendarran Warriors]], and the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] wished to capture the planet so that they could gain a significant advantage in the use of cloaking technology. Once the two factions attacked one another, however, [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] and [[Black Sun/Legends|Black Sun]] forces entered the system and destroyed the remainders of all three fleets. It is believed that the [[Dreighton Nebula/Legends|Dreighton Nebula]] itself eventually annihilated all combatants.

Whatever occurred there, it would soon be declared that there were no more stygium caches on Aeten II. The aftermath of the battle also had many rumors about the nebula being haunted afterwards with [[ghost ship]]s and the dead pilots of the battle, giving birth to the idea of the [[Dreighton Triangle]]. This was ratified by strange disappearances of ships flying in the nebula.

During the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], after the destruction of the first [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|Death Star]], [[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admiral]] [[Martio Batch]], wishing to recreate cloaking devices like the one used in the [[Scimitar/Legends|Sith Infiltrator]], brought the [[Tarkin (superweapon)|''Tarkin'']] to Aeten II, where the Stygium mines had dried up. The Admiral then used the ''Tarkin'' to destroy the planet and used the large supply of previously unreachable crystals to forward the [[TIE/ph "Phantom" Multi-Role Stealth Starfighter/Legends|Phantom TIE project]]. The planet stayed intact and habitable but had gashes leading to the core. It was in orbit of the ruins of Aeten II that the [[Executor-class Star Dreadnought/Legends|''Executor''-class Star Dreadnought]] ''[[Terror]]'', under [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Sarn]], protected the crystal supply.

His plan eventually failed when [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]] saboteurs [[Rookie One]] and [[Ru Murleen]] destroyed the ''[[Terror]]'', the corresponding [[Imdaar Alpha research station|TIE Phantom factory]] on [[Imdaar Alpha]] and all the TIE Phantoms.

==Behind the scenes==
Aeten II is present in the ''Empire at War'' story campaign, but not in the ''Forces of Corruption'' story campaign. This is consistent with the planet's destruction by the Tarkin superweapon after the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]]. However, the planet appears in ''Forces of Corruption's'' galactic conquest mode unchanged, which is acceptable because this game mode is not meant to be taken as canon.

The ''[[Star Wars: Empire at War: Prima Official Game Guide]]'' and ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'' incorrectly place Aeten II in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]. ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' has eventually stated that the system is in Wild Space. Some of the mission text for the Aeten Defense space mission in ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]'' mistakenly refers to the planet as Aeten Ten, while other instances in the text files correctly name it as Aeten II.
